CompedTake.description: One take a comped part drew from.

digest.description: The take's identity: the digest of its decoded samples.

reading.description:
The reader whose reading the notes are, such as `rules`, `hmm` or `basic-pitch`.
Absent for a rhythm take, which has one reading.

take.description: The take's name in the project, when it has one.

Control.description: A channel event other than a note.

oneOf.description: A control change, such as 64 for the sustain pedal or 1 for the mod wheel.
Pitch bend, from -8192 to 8191, with 0 as no bend.
A program change after the start of the track.

DocDigest.description: The 64-bit FNV-1a of the document's body as compact JSON, as 16 lowercase hex digits.

Key.description: A key such as D minor, Bb major or D dorian, with at most 7 sharps or flats.

Name.description: A name in the project: lowercase letters and digits, words joined by single hyphens, such as wayfaring or blood-sport-v2.

at.description: Where the note starts, as bar.beat.tick.

beats.description: The length in quarter notes, whatever the time signature.

PartBody.description: A part: its stable id, how it was made, and its notes and conductor, every field at one level.

end.description:
Where the part ends, if it says: a bar.beat.tick position such as `9.1.0` (the bar
line before bar 9), or one inside a bar, for a part that stops mid-bar. Nothing in
the part may lie past it: a note may end on it, and no note may end after it.

`None` means the part names no end, and its [default end](Part::default_end)
applies: the end of the last bar holding an event. Every writer states the end it
uses ([`Part::stated_end`]), so a written file always says where it ends, whatever
default computed it.

key.description: The key at the start, if the file names one.

tempo_bpm.description: The tempo at the start, in quarter notes per minute.

ticks_per_quarter.description: The file's resolution. Tick offsets in positions are counted in these ticks.

time_changes.description:
Time signature changes. Each one's position is read against the changes before it;
one that falls mid-bar cuts that bar short.

time_sig.description: The time signature at the start.

title.description:
The part's name: the MIDI sequence name, from the first track of a format 1 file
when that track holds no notes, or from the only track of a format 0 file.

PartBody.title: PartBody

Pitch.description: A pitch in scientific notation, such as C4 (MIDI 60), F#3, Bb2, Cb5 (MIDI 71) or F##4 (MIDI 67), from C-1 to G9: a letter, up to two sharps or two flats, and the letter's octave. Its spelling is kept.

Position.description: A position as bar.beat.tick, such as 3.2.240: bar and beat from 1, the tick an offset into the beat in the part's ticks. bar.beat alone is tick 0.

Source.description:
How a part was made (decision 01a1ee66, the songs spec's §2). Written as an object whose `by`
says which.

oneOf.description:
Written by hand, by the owner or by Claude: in duet, or in another program and imported
(the envelope's `from` says from what).

Comped from takes: a reading of each take it drew from, and the comp when there is one.
A take's reading kept as a part is a one-take comp with no comp: the simple case.

comp.description: The comp in the song's `comps/` that wrote the part, by its name.

takes.description: The takes the notes came from, at least one.

oneOf.description: Generated by an operation, which names itself and what it read, so it can be made again.

inputs.description: The digest of each document the operation read, in order.

operation.description: The operation, as its command names it, such as `drums render`.

TakeDigest.description: The SHA-256 of a take's decoded samples: the bytes `duet-take-1`, the rate as a little-endian u32, the channel count as a little-endian u16, then every sample, interleaved, as the little-endian bits of its f32.

TimeSig.description: A time signature such as 4/4 or 6/8: the denominator is 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64.

Track.description: One instrument part on one MIDI channel.

channel.description: The MIDI channel, 1 to 16 as DAWs number them.

controls.description: Controllers, pitch bends and later program changes, in the order they happen.

program.description: The General MIDI program (0 to 127) set at the start, if any.

description: A .duet document of kind part, at schema version 1.0.
title: duet part 1.0
